channel.title: Economics & Finance on [1697, 20747]
channel.description: Recent content in Economics & Finance on [1697, 20747]

item.title: The Royal Charter of the Bank of England (1694)
item.description: The founding document of modern public finance and central banking, establishing the world's first funded national debt.

item.title: Lombard Street
item.description: The foundational text on central banking. Written in 1873, Bagehot explains how the Bank of England should act as lender of last resort.

item.title: On Competition
item.description: Porter's collected essays on competitive strategy, clusters, and national competitiveness.

item.title: The Price of Time
item.description: A history of interest rates from ancient Mesopotamia to the post-2008 era of near-zero rates.

item.title: The Third Pillar
item.description: On the balance between state, market, and community. Rajan argues that economics has neglected the local community to its peril.

item.title: Keeping At It: The Quest for Sound Money and Good Government
item.description: Paul Volcker's memoir on his fight for sound money and the independence of central banks.

item.title: Euro
item.description: A rigorous critique of the eurozone's structural flaws from a Nobel laureate.

item.title: Financial Shenanigans
item.description: How companies manipulate earnings and cash flow statements. Forensic accounting made readable. Will permanently change how you read a 10-K.

item.title: Irrational Exuberance
item.description: The definitive account of speculative bubbles. Shiller called the dot-com peak and the housing crisis.
